review.note: Extracted as text from the old lesson, then reviewed against the verified dataset. A line with "review" set is held (not shown) until a teacher resolves it. Dropped: the five Tajweed rules, the two Tajweed quiz questions and the two Tajweed games (Tajweed comes only from the reviewed dataset), the audio URLs and the reciter line, the typed basmala and whole surah on the intro card, and every hand-typed Quran string (replaced by positions). The old quiz had difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard), not categories; the categories were assigned by question type. The four questions of the "listen and choose" game are carried into the quiz (q9-q12). The complete-the-ayah words are the answers of the four completion questions (two in the final quiz, two in the listen and choose game); the two-word answers became their last word. The old "complete the ayah" game hid a random word, so it has no fixed answers to carry. Each lesson learned is its old title and description joined with ": "; the lessons' "how we apply it" lines are the reflection's ideas, under the old second reflection question (the first and third questions and the "think about it with your parents" line are not carried). Not carried (no field or no such game in the engine): the intro facts (ayah count, "Makki") and the "story of the surah" paragraph, the intro quiz, the ayah-ordering and memory games, the word-to-meaning matching games and the meaning multiple-choice games (same words and meanings as the list and quiz). Matching aids, for alignment only and never stored: the old text writes ilafihim (2:1) with a full ya where the Uthmani text has a small ya; the word meaning al-sayf was typed without the wa- the verse word carries, so it points at the whole verse word (2:4).

intro.text: سورة قريش تتحدث عن نعم الله على قبيلة قريش، حيث كانوا يسافرون في الشتاء والصيف بأمان، وأمرهم الله أن يعبدوه ويشكروه على نعمه الكثيرة.

tafsir.text: لأن الله جعل قريشاً يعتادون ويألفون شيئاً جميلاً...
tafsir.review: The line trails off ("... something beautiful...") and leaves ayah 2 to say what Quraysh were accustomed to. Common tafsir: li-ilaf is "for the accustoming / security of Quraysh", tied either to Al-Fil (Allah repelled the army for the sake of Quraysh's ilaf) or to "let them worship" in ayah 3. Teacher to confirm the line reads as a whole for a child.

tafsir.text: كانوا يسافرون رحلتين: رحلة في الشتاء إلى اليمن الدافئة، ورحلة في الصيف إلى الشام الباردة، للتجارة وجلب الطعام.
فليشكروا الله ويعبدوه وحده، فهو رب الكعبة المشرفة الذي حماهم ورزقهم.
الله هو الذي أعطاهم الطعام عندما كانوا جائعين، وجعلهم آمنين ولا يخافون من أي شيء.

words.meaning: اسم القبيلة التي كانت تعيش في مكة

words.review: Gives "let them obey and give thanks". The word means "let them worship"; common tafsir: let them single out the Lord of this House in worship (in thanks for the two journeys). The lesson's own tafsir of ayah 3 says "let them thank Allah and worship Him alone". Teacher to align the wording.
PHRASE: the old entry is the two words "hadha al-bayt" (3:3-4); the engine shows one word, so this points at al-bayt (3:4) and the meaning covers both. Teacher to confirm it reads right.

lessons.text: شكر الله على النعم: الله أعطانا نعماً كثيرة: الطعام، الأمان، العائلة. يجب أن نقول 'الحمد لله' دائماً!
عبادة الله وحده: الله هو الذي يرزقنا ويحمينا، لذلك نعبده وحده ونصلي له.
الأمان نعمة كبيرة: أن نعيش بأمان في بيوتنا وبلادنا نعمة عظيمة من الله.
مساعدة المحتاجين: كما أطعم الله قريشاً من جوع، علينا أن نساعد من يحتاج الطعام.
lessons.review: Helping the needy is a good lesson, but the surah does not teach it: it reminds Quraysh that Allah fed them and made them safe, so they should worship Him. This lesson draws it by analogy. Teacher to keep or drop.

reflection.question: كيف يمكن أن نشكر الله على نعمه كل يوم؟
ideas: كل يوم قبل النوم، اذكر 3 نعم أعطاك الله إياها وقل الحمد لله.
حافظ على صلاتك وادعُ الله في كل وقت.
اشكر الله على أنك تعيش في أمان مع عائلتك.
شارك طعامك مع أصدقائك وساعد من يحتاج.
